'''Jalen Devonn Williams''' (born April 14, 2001), nicknamed '''J-Dub''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played three seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara Broncos]] before declaring for the [[2022 NBA draft]], where he was selected 12th overall by the Thunder. Williams was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] and [[All-NBA Team]] in 2025, later winning an [[NBA champion]]ship that same year.

==High school career==
Williams played basketball at [[Perryton High School (Perryton, Texas)|Perry High School]] in [[Gilbert, Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thompson |first=Marcus II |date=2025-06-20 |title=Jalen Williams’ NBA Finals breakout powered by years of hard work and conviction |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6431634/2025/06/17/jalen-williams-nba-finals-game-5/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Thunder’s Jalen Williams gets street named after him at Arizona alma mater |url=https://www.newson6.com/story/6853fe22f9bf981a12e717e6/okc-thunder-jalen-williams-street-name-arizona |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=newson6.com |language=en}}</ref> Starting off as a {{convert|6|ft|cm|-tall|adj=mid|spell=in}} point guard, Williams grew five inches from his sophomore to senior year of high school. Despite this, [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] still listed him as a {{height|ft=6|in=3}} guard when Williams signed his national letter of intent.<ref name="x622">{{cite web | last=Greabell | first=Grant | title=Jalen Williams receiving NBA buzz amid breakout basketball season | website=Cronkite News | date=2022-02-14 | url=https://cronkitenews.azpbs.org/2022/02/14/jalen-williams-receiving-nba-buzz-breakout-basketball-season/ | access-date=2025-03-09}}</ref> As a senior, Williams was ranked 9th among prep players in Arizona by [[247Sports]]. Williams ended his high school career averaging more than 25 points per game in his senior year, being named the Chandler Unified School District Player of the Year as a junior, and was awarded the 2017–18 Region Offensive Player of the Year.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography">{{cite web|title=Santa Clara Broncos: JALEN WILLIAMS's Bio|url=https://www.santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/bios/williams_jalen_loag|website=santaclarabroncos.com|access-date=May 27, 2022|archive-date=June 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220624122304/https://santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/bios/williams_jalen_loag|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Rated as a three-star recruit by major recruiting services [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], Williams committed to [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] over offers from [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]] and [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].<ref>{{cite web|title=247Sports: Jalen Williams's Recruiting|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jalen-Williams-46047744/high-school-202409/|website=247sports.com}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 5, 2019, Williams made his debut for [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]], recording 13 points, 5 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals against [[University of California, Santa Cruz|UC Santa Cruz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=UC Santa Cruz vs. Santa Clara Box Score (Men), November 5, 2019|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2019-11-05-22-santa-clara.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> As a freshman, Williams played in all 33 games, starting in the final 23 games while leading the team in steals with 44—which ranked third on the school's all-time freshman list.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/> Against [[Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils men's basketball|Mississippi Valley State]], Williams had season bests with 19 points, 7 rebounds and career highs in field goals, three-pointers and assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mississippi Valley State vs. Santa Clara Box Score (Men), December 20, 2019|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2019-12-20-22-santa-clara.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> He finished his freshman season averaging 7.7 points in 25.5 minutes. In his sophomore season, Williams started in all of his 18 appearances and was second on the team in scoring and free throw percentage.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/> In the opening round of the [[2021 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2021 WCC tournament]], Williams recorded his first career double-double with 13 points and a career-high 10 rebounds against [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]] in a 78–70 loss.<ref>{{cite web|title=Santa Clara vs. Pepperdine Box Score (Men), March 6, 2021|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2021-03-06-23-pepperdine.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> He increased his scoring average to 11.5 points in 31.6 minutes in his sophomore season.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/>

In his final season with Santa Clara, Williams emerged as a scorer, finishing second in the WCC with 18.0 points per game while shooting 51.3%. In 31 out of 33 games, Williams scored in double figures including scoring 16 or more points in 21 games.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/> Against [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors men's basketball|Hawaii]], Williams registered a career-high 30 points with four rebounds and four assists on November 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawaii vs. Santa Clara Box Score (Men), November 30, 2021|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2021-11-30-21-santa-clara.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> On January 27, 2022, Williams hit a game-winning shot against [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] while finishing with 26 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brigham Young vs. Santa Clara Box Score (Men), January 27, 2022|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2022-01-27-23-santa-clara.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> On March 15, 2022, in the [[2022 National Invitation Tournament|2022 NIT]], Williams played his final collegiate game, finishing with 19 points, 15 rebounds and 4 assists in a 63–50 loss against [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Santa Clara vs. Washington State Box Score (Men), March 15, 2022|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2022-03-15-23-washington-state.html|website=sports-reference.com}}</ref> At the end of the season, Williams was named as a First Team All-WCC selection, Second Team NABC All-District, and was named as a finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], given to the nation's top mid-major player.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/>

As a three-year guard, Williams finished his collegiate career as a two-time All-WCC choice and reached 1,000 career points as a junior after averaging 12.6 points on 46.9% shooting for his career.<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/> On March 31, 2022, Williams declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jalen Williams To Test The NBA Draft Waters|url=https://www.santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/releases/20220331mui9kj|website=santaclarabroncos.com|date=March 31, 2022|access-date=June 25, 2023|archive-date=April 19, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419180533/https://www.santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/releases/20220331mui9kj|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder (2022–present)===
Described as a long, smooth small forward who can score on strong efficiency numbers while showing a sense of urgency and can use his length to contest shots, Williams was drafted 12th overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]] with a pick the Thunder acquired from the Clippers in the 2019 [[Paul George]] trade.<ref>{{cite web|title=2022 NBA DRAFT PROFILE: Jalen Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2022/prospects/jalen-williams|website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Welcomes 2022 Draft Class|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/story-draftclass-220624|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2022}}</ref> With the selection, Williams became the first Santa Clara player to be drafted since [[Steve Nash]] in 1996. He is currently the highest-drafted Bronco prospect in the modern era and the second highest in Santa Clara history behind [[Ken Sears]] in 1955.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jalen Williams Selected 12th Overall In 2022 NBA Draft|url=https://www.santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/releases/20220623wirli7|website=santaclarabroncos.com|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=June 25, 2023|archive-date=June 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220624121938/https://www.santaclarabroncos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2021-22/releases/20220623wirli7|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2022–2023: All-Rookie honors====
On October 19, 2022, Williams made his NBA debut, putting up 5 points in 6 minutes before taking a hit defending a dunk attempt by [[Jaden McDaniels]]. He would leave the game and later undergo surgery to address a right orbital bone fracture.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder's Jalen Williams has surgery for orbital bone fracture|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34846677|website=ESPN.com|date=October 21, 2022|access-date=July 21, 2026|last=MacMahon|first=Tim}}</ref> After missing four games, Williams started sporadically for the Thunder until forward [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]] suffered a right ankle sprain which made him the full-time starter. With guard [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]] sidelined, Williams scored 27 points and helped rallied the Thunder from a 20-point second-half deficit against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on November 30, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs vs Thunder - November 30, 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200319|website=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2022}}</ref> The next day, he was named NBA Rookie of the Month for October/November after averaging 10.7 points on 52.4% shooting, 3.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists. He became the third Thunder rookie to win Rookie of the Month honors after [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Josh Giddey]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jalen Williams, Bennedict Mathurin named Kia Rookies of the Month|url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-rookies-of-the-month-oct-nov-2022-23|website=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2022}}</ref> 

On January 31, 2023, Williams was named to the [[2023 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|2023 Rising Stars Challenge]] after averaging 12.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.7 steals in 46 games. Against the [[Utah Jazz]], Williams recorded a career-high 32 points on 12–15 shooting in a 129–119 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz vs Thunder - March 5, 2023|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200968|website=NBA.com|date=March 5, 2023}}</ref> Without Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams was one point shy of tying his then career high with 31 points along with 4 steals in a 137–134 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets vs Thunder - March 28, 2023|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022201134|website=NBA.com|date=March 28, 2023}}</ref> After the Thunder fell two games under .500, Williams had a putback with less than a second in a 107–106 win after [[Josh Giddey]]'s hook shot rolled off. He led the Thunder with 27 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists and joined [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Russell Westbrook]] to have three or more games with at least 25 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists in a season as a rookie.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pistons vs Thunder - March 29, 2023|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022201142|website=NBA.com|date=March 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Only 3 rookies in Thunder history have 3 games with 25+ PTS, 5+ AST, and 5+ REB: Kevin Durant, Russell Westbrook, Jalen Williams|url=https://x.com/NBAHistory/status/1641267563383455749|website=x.com|date=March 29, 2023}}</ref> Williams was later named his second NBA Rookie of the Month award for March and April.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paolo Banchero, Jalen Williams named Kia NBA Rookies of the Month|url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-rookies-of-month-paolo-banchero-jalen-williams|website=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2023}}</ref> In his rookie season, Williams averaged 14.1 points on 52% shooting and finished second in [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting with 75 second place votes and 16 third place votes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paolo Banchero named 2022-23 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year|url=https://www.nba.com/news/paolo-banchero-named-2022-23-kia-nba-rookie-of-the-year|website=NBA.com|date=April 25, 2023}}</ref> Williams was later named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] becoming the second Thunder player to be named to it and the fifth Thunder player overall to be named to an All-Rookie team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jalen Williams Named to All-Rookie First Team|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-allrookie-230508|website=NBA.com|date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

====2023–2024: First playoff appearance====
On December 27, 2023, Williams scored a career-high 36 points in a 129–120 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-jalen-williams-efficient-game-knicks-never-been-seen-before|title=Jalen Williams' efficient game in Thunder vs. Knicks has never been seen before|website=ClutchPoints|last=Postrado|first=Jay|date=December 28, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023}}</ref> On January 23, 2024, Williams put up 19 points alongside a game-winning jump shot in a 111–109 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-jalen-williams-brutally-honest-shooting-like-trash-before-game-winner|title=Thunder's Jalen Williams gets brutally honest on shooting like 'trash' before game-winner|website=ClutchPoints|last=House|first=Alex|date=January 23, 2024|access-date=January 23, 2024}}</ref> Williams helped lead the Thunder to a 57–25 record and their first Western Conference first seed since 2013, entering the [[2024 NBA playoffs]]. It was also his first playoff appearance.

In his playoff debut on April 21, 2024, Williams recorded 19 points, seven rebounds, four assists and two steals in a 94–92 Game 1 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the opening round of the NBA playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 22, 2024 |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 28 points as top-seeded Thunder edge Pelicans 94-92 in Game 1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401654762 |access-date=April 22, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> The Thunder advanced to the Conference Semifinals but were eliminated in six games by the [[Dallas Mavericks]], despite Williams' near triple-double performance in the final game, where he had 22 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and zero turnovers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 18, 2024 |title=P.J. Washington's free throws finish rally as Mavericks beat Thunder 117-116 to reach West finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401658194 |access-date=May 25, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

====2024–2025: First All-Star selection, All-NBA honors and NBA championship====
On January 30, 2025, Williams was named as reserve for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his first selection.<ref>{{cite web |title= Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves |website=NBA.com |date=January 30, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves |access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> On March 2, Williams scored a career-high 41 points along with six rebounds and six assists in a 146–132 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder spoil Spurs' homecoming with 146-132 victory behind career-high 41 points by Williams|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705437|website=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2025}}</ref> At the end of the season, Williams was named to the [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Third Team]], marking his first career All-NBA selection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 24, 2025 |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić, Giannis Antetokounmpo anchor 2024-25 Kia All-NBA Team |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-25-all-nba-teams-announced |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> He was also named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]], another first in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 23, 2025 |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić, Giannis Antetokounmpo anchor 2024-25 Kia All-NBA Team |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-25-all-defensive-teams-announced |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

Williams attracted criticism for his offensive performance during the Western Conference Semifinals against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Mussatto |first=Joe |date=2025-05-16 |title=OKC Thunder needs more from Jalen Williams to oust Nuggets from NBA Playoffs in Game 7 |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2025/05/16/okc-thunder-vs-denver-nuggets-jalen-williams-stats-game-7-schedule/83656908007/ |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Excluding Game 2, in which he posted 17 points and seven assists in a 149–106 blowout win,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zillgitt |first=Jeff |date=2025-05-08 |title=Nuggets-Thunder Game 2 winners, losers: OKC rides record-setting first half to blowout win |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2025/05/07/nuggets-thunder-game-2/83505834007/ |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=[[USA Today]] |language=en-US}}</ref> and Game 3 when he scored a team-high 32 points in a 113–104 overtime defeat,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-10 |title=Murray and Porter lead the Nuggets to a 113-104 bounce-back win over the Thunder |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401769822 |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Williams shot a combined 24% from the field and 21% from behind the three-point-line from Game 1 through 6. He faced particular scrutiny for his outing in Game 6, in which he posted just six points on 3-of-16 shooting in a 119–107 loss.<ref name=":0"/> He bounced back in Game 7 however, scoring 24 points in a 125–93 victory over the Nuggets, eliminating them and allowing him his first Western Conference Finals appearance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-19 |title=Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder oust Nuggets, move on to NBA West finals |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/5/19/thunder-vs-nuggets-okc-win-game-7-reach-western-conference-finals |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=[[Al Jazeera]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 26, in Game 4 of the [[2025 NBA playoffs#(1) Oklahoma City Thunder vs. (6) Minnesota Timberwolves|Western Conference Finals]], Williams scored a then-playoff career-high 34 points, helping the Thunder to a 128–126 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and a 3–1 lead in the series.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2025 |title=Thunder bounce back to beat T-wolves 128-126 to take 3-1 lead behind SGA's 40-point game. Obliterated Wolves in game 5 help secure OKC in the NBA Finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401773151 |access-date=May 27, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> After the Thunder won the series in five games, they advanced to the NBA Finals for the first time since 2012, marking the first Finals appearance of Williams' career.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oklahoma City Thunder beat Minnesota Timberwolves 124-94 to win Western Conference 4-1 and reach NBA Finals win|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401773152|date=May 29, 2025|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In Game 5 of the [[2025 NBA Finals]] against the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]], Williams scored a new playoff career-high 40 points in a 120–109 victory to give the Thunder a 3–2 lead in the series. He became the third-youngest player to score at least 40 points in a Finals game, trailing only [[Magic Johnson]] and [[Russell Westbrook]]. Williams also recorded at least 25 points and five rebounds in three consecutive NBA Finals games, becoming the first player under the age of 25 to achieve such a streak since [[Shaquille O'Neal]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacMahon |first=Tim |date=June 17, 2025 |title='Really gutsy' Jalen Williams fuels Thunder in Game 5 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45528511 |access-date=December 11, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Marcus II |date=2025-06-18 |title=The Athletic: Jalen Williams’ NBA Finals breakout powered by years of hard work and conviction |url=https://www.nba.com/news/the-athletic-jalen-williams-nba-finals-breakout-powered-by-years-of-hard-work-and-conviction |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Oklahoma City won the series 4–3, with Williams contributing 20 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals in the decisive Game 7.<ref>{{cite news |last=Owens |first=Jason |title=NBA Finals Game 7: Thunder beat Pacers for NBA title behind big game from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander after injury to Tyrese Haliburton |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/live/nba-finals-game-7-thunder-beat-pacers-for-nba-title-behind-big-game-from-shai-gilgeous-alexander-after-injury-to-tyrese-haliburton-223022939.html |access-date=June 22, 2025 |work=Yahoo Sports |date=June 22, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|title=How Oklahoma City's Jalen Williams became this generation's Scottie Pippen|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45540348|date=June 19, 2025|website=ESPN.com|author-link=Tim MacMahon}}</ref> Williams revealed that he received about 30 painkilling injections in his injured right wrist during the [[2025 NBA playoffs]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Windhorst |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Windhorst |date=July 9, 2025 |title=Jalen Williams Endured Nearly 30 Painkilling Injections To Play Through Wrist Injury |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/281320/Jalen-Williams-Endured-Nearly-30-Painkilling-Injections-To-Play-Through-Wrist-Injury |access-date=July 9, 2025 |work=Real GM}}</ref> On June 30, it was announced that he would undergo surgery to repair a torn ligament in the same wrist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jalen Williams to have surgery on right wrist after playing through injury in Thunder's title run|url=https://www.nba.com/news/jalen-williams-wrist-surgery-after-thunder-championship|access-date=August 25, 2025|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2025|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2025–2026: Contract extension and injury-riddled season====
On July 13, 2025, Williams signed a five-year contract extension that could be worth $287 million with the Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder Signs Jalen Williams to Multi-Year Contract Extension|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-williams-250713|date=July 13, 2025}}</ref> During the regular season, Williams missed more than half of the games due to injury issues. In the playoffs, Williams and the Thunder were eliminated by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in seven games in the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(1) Oklahoma City Thunder vs. (2) San Antonio Spurs|Western Conference Finals]]. He also missed several postseason games due to injury and did not play in Game 7, which the Thunder lost 111–103.<ref>{{cite web |title=4 Takeaways: Spurs advance to Finals after Game 7 win over Thunder |url=https://www.nba.com/news/4-takeaways-spurs-thunder-game-7 |website=NBA.com |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
In preparation for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], Williams was selected to the [[United States men's national basketball team|2023 USA Basketball Men's Select team]] alongside Thunder teammate [[Chet Holmgren]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Holmgren and Williams Named to USA Select Team|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-usaselect-230724|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams was born in [[Denver|Denver, Colorado]], but moved to [[Gilbert, Arizona]] when he was 7 years old. His parents – Ronald and Nicole Williams – were both members of the [[United States Air Force]]. His younger brother, [[Cody Williams]], was a consensus five-star recruit who plays for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref name="Santa Clara: Jalen William Biography"/>

Williams is also an investor in [[USL Championship]] soccer club [[OKC Energy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestadiumbusiness.com/2026/06/26/baker-mayfield-jalen-williams-join-growing-list-of-okc-for-soccer-investors/|title=Baker Mayfield, Jalen Williams join growing list of OKC for Soccer investors|first=Owen|last=Lloyd|date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>
